doc.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020

title: Music at home growing up: radio and non-musical parents
summary: Parents were supportive but not musical; the only music was a radio station playing pop, Bing Crosby and some Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Can you tell me what kind of music you heard in your house growing up? You were —
You mean in the house growing up with my parents?
Whatever was on the radio. Other than that, you know.
So they didn’t have a record player?
No. Neither of my parents were musically inclined.

They were very supportive of my sister and I as parents, but they were not really musically inclined. So there was a radio station, the call letters was WJBW, and it was the only radio station that actually played music. And it would change I think, as I remember during the day. As it got later in the evening there would be different kinds of music, some orchestral types of music. I don’t know that they ever actually played some symphonies but earlier in the day they would play recordings of like Bing Crosby and maybe Louis Armstrong. And — but it wasn’t — it was sort of like the Broadway-pop kind of music.
